Ingestion of eggs (e.g., from contaminated food or water) can lead to cysticercosis, a more serious condition.

qs.q: How do humans typically acquire cysticercosis caused by the larval stage of Taenia solium?
o: Ingesting undercooked pork containing cysticerci in muscle
Handling infected dogs and inhaling shed parasite oncospheres
Ingesting T. solium eggs via auto-infection or food
Consuming raw freshwater fish containing plerocercoid larvae
qs.e: Cysticercosis occurs when humans ingest T. solium eggs, often through auto-infection or contaminated food, leading to tissue-invasive larvae. Ingestion of undercooked pork containing cysticerci leads to adult intestinal taeniasis instead.

qs.q: Which part of the human body is not inhabited by the larvae in cysticercosis? ---
qs.e: Cysticercus larvae can inhabit various organs including the brain, liver, lungs, and kidneys, making none of the listed organs completely exempt.
